title: S3: buckets, objects, prefixes and a naming scheme that survives

videos.script: This course follows the data of one company. Quitanda delivers groceries in São Paulo, and every night its shop exports the day's orders. {{export}} Those files have to land somewhere. They have to stay for years, be read by the right people and by nobody else, and cost as little as they can. That is S3, and it is the first five lessons. {{s3}} You will practise all of it on your own computer. There is no AWS account in this course. The real AWS command line talks to moto, a program that imitates AWS, on a port of your laptop. {{moto}} moto answers like AWS and checks much less. This lesson shows you exactly where the imitation ends, so that a success never fools you. {{limits}} Then the first bucket. You will put three files in it and find that the folders you see are not there at all. {{folders}} And you will choose names for buckets and keys that still make sense in five years, because in S3 nothing can be renamed. {{names}}
